title: Accessibility of a small-generated strongly saturated arrow class
statement: Use universes and presentable infinity categories from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and coherent functor categories from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal C$ be presentable and let $S$ be a small set of its arrows. A class of arrows is replete if it is invariant under equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$. Let $W$ be the smallest replete class containing $S$ and all equivalences, closed under pushouts and all small colimits in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$, and satisfying two-out-of-three for composable arrows. Then the full subcategory $\mathcal A_W\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$ spanned by $W$ is accessible. Its inclusion preserves all small colimits, which exist and are computed as in the ambient arrow category.

source.place: HTT Lemma 5.5.4.14, implication (3) to (1), printed pp. 480-481; colimit closure is part of strong saturation. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical theorem.

proof.text: Choose $\lambda<\kappa$ by [lem-coef-presentable-cardinal-enlargement]. In particular $\kappa$ is uncountable, $\lambda$ is sharply smaller in the explicitly stated cardinal sense, $\mathcal C$ is accessible at both cardinals, and all generator endpoints are $\kappa$-compact. Write $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$ and let $\mathcal D_0$ be the replete full subcategory of arrows of $W$ with $\kappa$-compact endpoints. It is essentially small: [lem-coef-presentable-cardinal-enlargement] bounds the equivalence classes of endpoints, and local smallness bounds the components of each mapping space of arrows between chosen endpoints. Colimits in $\mathcal E$ exist and are computed at the two endpoints by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. For a $\kappa$-small diagram in $\mathcal D_0$, its colimit arrow is in $W$ by the definition of $W$, and its two endpoints are $\kappa$-compact by [lem-coef-compact-small-colimits]. Thus $\mathcal D_0$ is closed under $\kappa$-small colimits.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14, p. 480, choice of cardinal and compact-endpoint subcategory; Proposition 5.4.2.2(2).

proof.text: By the compactness clause of [lem-coef-accessible-diagram-presentations] with $K=\Delta^1$, all objects of $\mathcal D_0$ are $\kappa$-compact in $\mathcal E$. Define $\mathcal D_1$ as their replete full $\kappa$-filtered-colimit hull in $\mathcal E$. Applying [lem-coef-accessible-ind-colimit-extension] proves that $\mathcal D_1$ is $\kappa$-accessible and closed under all small ambient colimits, including the empty colimit. It also supplies a presentation of each object of $\mathcal D_1$ by $\mathcal D_0$ indexed by a small $\kappa$-filtered poset. The ambient category $\mathcal E$ is $\kappa$-accessible by [lem-coef-accessible-diagram-presentations] with $K=\Delta^1$ and has all small colimits by Step 1; it is therefore presentable by [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], as the hull lemma requires. Let $W_1$ be the arrows represented by $\mathcal D_1$.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14, p. 480, filtered hull and its colimit closure.

proof.text: Every arrow of $\mathcal D_0$ belongs to $W$, and $W$ is closed under the filtered arrow colimits and equivalences used to form $\mathcal D_1$; hence $W_1\subseteq W$. The generator endpoints chosen in Step 1 are $\kappa$-compact, so $S\subseteq\mathcal D_0\subseteq W_1$. It remains to prove pushout stability and two-out-of-three for $W_1$. Its repleteness and closure under all small arrow colimits already follow from its definition and Step 2.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14, p. 480, reduction to strong saturation.

proof.text: Let $K$ be either $\Lambda^2_0$ or $\Delta^2$, and fix a diagram $p:K\to\mathcal C$ and an edge $e$ with $p(e)\in W_1$. By [lem-coef-accessible-diagram-presentations], choose a presentation $q:N(A)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ of $p$ by pointwise $\kappa$-compact diagrams, where $A$ is small and $\kappa$-filtered. Apply [lem-coef-compact-presentation-functor-refinement] with $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$, $\mathcal F=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$, $H$ restriction to $e$, and $\mathcal P=\mathcal D_0$. Both categories are locally small and admit all small colimits: accessibility is supplied by [lem-coef-accessible-diagram-presentations], and colimits are pointwise by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. The compactness clause of the diagram lemma makes $q(a)$ compact in $\mathcal E$ and $Hq(a)$ compact in $\mathcal F$. Step 1 gives closure of $\mathcal D_0$ under $\kappa$-small colimits, and Step 2 supplies the required presentation of $H(p)$. We obtain a small $\kappa$-filtered poset $B$ of $\kappa$-small filtered subsets of $A$ and a presentation $q'(b)=\operatorname{colim}_{N(b)}q$ of $p$ whose $e$-edge lies in $\mathcal D_0$. Its vertex values are compact by pointwise computation and [lem-coef-compact-small-colimits]; $N(b)$ is $\kappa$-small since $\kappa$ is uncountable regular.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14, printed p. 481, replacement of A by the good partial-colimit poset B; generic refinement isolated as a separate node.

proof.text: This replacement also preserves an edge $d$ already lying in $\mathcal D_0$ at every stage of the supplied presentation $q$: its value at the new stage $b$ is the $N(b)$-colimit of those old edge values. Since $N(b)$ is $\kappa$-small, Step 1 puts this colimit in $\mathcal D_0$. Consequently Step 4 applies to any supplied pointwise compact presentation and may be repeated for a second edge while retaining the first.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14, printed pp. 481-482, repeated refinement retains the previously constrained edge.

proof.text:
Write $A_s=\{a\le b,a\le c\}$ for the span poset and $B_s=A_s\cup\{d\}$ with $b,c\le d$ for the square poset. By [lem-coef-infinity-finite-poset-kan-extension], restriction $j^*$ along $j:A_s\subset B_s$ has a functorial left adjoint $j_!$, because $\mathcal C$ has finite colimits. It extends each span to its pushout square, since $(j_!H)(d)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{A_s}H$. This left adjoint preserves the filtered colimits of spans under consideration: for every square $T$, adjunction and the mapping-space colimit criterion in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] give
$$\operatorname{Map}(j_!\operatorname{colim}_i p_i,T)\simeq\lim_{i\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}(p_i,j^*T)\simeq\lim_{i\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}(j_!p_i,T).$$
The equivalences are natural in $T$ and in the cocone. Evaluation at $b\to d$ preserves colimits by the same node's pointwise computation. Hence the pushout arrow of a filtered colimit of spans is the filtered colimit of their pushout arrows.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14, printed p. 481, coherent pushout functor; Lemma 5.5.2.3.

proof.text: For a span $X'\leftarrow X\xrightarrow fY$ with $f\in W_1$, apply Step 4 to $f$. This gives pointwise compact spans $X'_b\leftarrow X_b\xrightarrow{f_b}Y_b$ with $f_b\in\mathcal D_0$. Pushout stability of $W$ puts $f'_b:X'_b\to X'_b\amalg_{X_b}Y_b$ in $W$. Its endpoints are compact by [lem-coef-compact-small-colimits], so $f'_b\in\mathcal D_0$. Step 6 identifies the original pushout arrow with the filtered colimit of the $f'_b$. It therefore lies in $W_1$ by its definition. Thus $W_1$ is pushout-stable.

Step 2 includes the initial arrow $0\to0$ in $W_1$. Its pushout along $0\to X$ is $\mathrm{id}_X$, so Step 7 puts every identity in $W_1$. For an equivalence $f:X\to Y$, the natural square from $\mathrm{id}_X$ to $f$ with components $\mathrm{id}_X,f$ is pointwise an equivalence. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] it is an equivalence in the arrow category. Repleteness of $W_1$ therefore puts every equivalence in $W_1$.

source.place: Remark 5.5.4.6, printed p. 477; pointwise equivalences in functor categories, Corollary 5.1.2.3.

proof.text: Let $p:\Delta^2\to\mathcal C$ have edges $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$, and $h:X\to Z$, with its specified coherent composition $gf\simeq h$. If $f,g\in W_1$, apply Step 4 first to $f$ and then to $g$. This yields pointwise $\kappa$-compact triangles whose $f$- and $g$-edges are in $\mathcal D_0$. Two-out-of-three for $W$ puts their $h$-edges in $W$; compactness of the vertices puts these edges in $\mathcal D_0$. Their filtered colimit is $h$ by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], so $h\in W_1$. If $f,h\in W_1$, refine first the $f$-edge and then the $h$-edge; two-out-of-three in $W$ gives the $g$-edge at each compact stage, and evaluation gives $g\in W_1$ on taking the filtered colimit. If $g,h\in W_1$, refine first the $g$-edge and then the $h$-edge; two-out-of-three in $W$ gives the $f$-edge at each compact stage, and its filtered colimit gives $f\in W_1$. In both repeated refinements Step 5 preserves the first edge.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14, pp. 481-482, all three two-out-of-three cases.

proof.text: The replete class $W_1$ contains $S$ and every equivalence, is closed under all small arrow colimits and pushouts, and satisfies two-out-of-three by Steps 2-9. The defining minimality of $W$ gives $W\subseteq W_1$; Step 3 gives the reverse inclusion. Thus $\mathcal A_W=\mathcal D_1$. Its accessibility and closure under all small ambient arrow colimits are Step 2. For each such colimit, fullness identifies the mapping-space universal property in the subcategory with the ambient one, so the inclusion preserves it and the colimits are computed as claimed.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14 (3)⇒(1), conclusion; closure under colimits is Definition 5.5.4.5(2).
